newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo banks post modest Q3 operating profit.
newsitem.headline: Yugo banks post modest Q3 operating profit.

text.p: Yugoslav banks posted a 76.7 million dinar ($14.95 million) after-tax operating profit during the third quarter 1996, the Yugoslav Banking Association (YBA) said on Friday in its latest quarterly report.
The results come as a modest relief after 96 out of 115 Yugoslav banks had reported a 103.5 million dinar loss over the second quarter of the year.
Banks continued their cyclical performance. Their lending activity remained modest, with up to 30 percent of total expenditures to be written off, the YBA report said.
"Most banks perform with losses. The only encouraging thing was that December-on-December inflation will not exceed 60 percent," Biljana Seskar of YBA told Reuters.
Seskar blamed a tough central bank stance and its decision to curb M1 money supply and halt a reportedly expanding credit activity by launching a 15 percent reserve requirement.

"Banks had to set aside several hundred million dinars with 2.5 percent interest on deposited funds. But since they have no alternative capital they must borrow from the same source and pay a 13 percent interest on those funds," she said.
According to YBA figures, out of 92 reporting banks, 59 posted profit totalling 413.7 million dinars, while thirty of them reported a total of 337 million dinar losses.
One of the reporting banks alone had a 120 million dinar loss.
Total banking sector income for the January-September period totalled 7.399 billion dinars while expenditures stood at 7.015 billion, the report said.
Banks had to set aside 305 million dinars for the reserve requirement introduced early in September.
YBA statistics for the third quarter showed total assets of the banking sector at 72.528 billion dinars with hard currency funds accounting for 58.8 billion of the total.
Dinar sight deposits totalled 2.49 billion, up from 1.72 billion at the end of the first quarter, while hard currency sight deposits declined to 11.510 from 12.270 billion dinars.
Dinar short-term deposits rose to 1.218 billion from 763 million, while hard currency short-term deposits dropped to 1.575 from 1.846 billion dinars.
The YBA report showed a sharp decline in dinar long-term deposits to 86 from 109 million dinars, while long-term hard currency deposits fell to 10.763 billion from 11.041 billion dinars.
